Record Class PythonReactiveContext

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.micronaut.context.python.PythonReactiveContext
Record Components:
reactorContext - The Reactor reactor.util.context.Context of the subscriber, or null when Reactor is not on the class path or the coroutine was started eagerly; typed as an object so the record loads without Reactor
propagatedContext - The propagated context of the subscriber or caller
@Internal public record PythonReactiveContext(@Nullable Object reactorContext, PropagatedContext propagatedContext) extends Record
The reactive context a subscriber (or the caller of an eager coroutine) hands to a Python coroutine: the Reactor context of the subscription (a reactive transaction status lives there) and the propagated context it carries. The asyncio task keeps it in a contextvars variable, so every publisher the coroutine awaits is subscribed within it and every callback of the task runs in its propagated context, whichever thread or task scheduled the callback.
Since:
5.2.0

  • Method Details

    • inheriting

      public PythonReactiveContext inheriting(PythonReactiveContext enclosing)
      The context of a coroutine started inside a task: this one, with the Reactor context of the enclosing task when this one has none (an eager start carries the propagated context of the caller only, and a nested coroutine must subscribe within the enclosing transaction). The propagated context of the caller is written into the inherited Reactor context, so a publisher looking it up there (a reactive transaction, tracing) finds the same context the thread runs in rather than the one of the enclosing subscription.
      Parameters:
      enclosing - The reactive context of the task the coroutine is started from
      Returns:
      The context of the new task
